subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Europa: An Ocean World
description: A micro-lesson that makes Europa: An Ocean World usable.

hook.text: Europa's smooth, icy surface hides a global ocean of liquid water—twice the volume of all Earth's oceans combined.

buildup.text: The ice shell is perhaps 15–25 km thick. Below it, a salt-water ocean extends down to a rocky seafloor.

discovery.text: Galileo spacecraft data revealed an induced magnetic field—a signature of a conductive liquid (salt water) beneath the ice.

twist.text: Reddish-brown streaks on the surface may be salts from the ocean below—delivered by cryovolcanism or ice convection.

climax.text: Europa is the top candidate for finding extraterrestrial life in our solar system. The ocean has water, heat, and chemistry.

punchline.text: Twice Earth's water, under a shell of ice. The ocean most likely to harbor alien life.

quiz.question: How did scientists confirm Europa has a subsurface ocean?
options: The Galileo spacecraft detected an induced magnetic field from conductive salt water
They observed liquid water erupting from large surface cracks
Infrared telescopes measured heat rising from under the ice

details.summary: Europa, Jupiter's ice-covered moon, harbors a global saltwater ocean beneath its frozen shell, likely containing twice the water of all Earth's oceans. Tidal heating from Jupiter keeps the ocean liquid.
details.whyItMatters: Europa may have all the ingredients for life: liquid water, energy from tidal heating, and potentially chemical nutrients from the rocky seafloor. It's the solar system's top candidate for finding life beyond Earth.
takeaways: Global saltwater ocean beneath an ice shell
Contains roughly twice the water of Earth's oceans
Top candidate for extraterrestrial life in the solar system

faq.question: How do we know Europa has an ocean?
faq.answer: Galileo spacecraft magnetic field measurements showed Europa's magnetic signature changes as it orbits Jupiter — consistent with a conducting layer (saltwater) beneath the ice. Europa's young, cracked surface suggests internal activity.

faq.question: How thick is Europa's ice shell?
faq.answer: Estimates range from 10 to 30 km, with significant uncertainty. Some regions may be thinner where geologic activity is strongest. Tidal flexing cracks the ice, creating the characteristic ridges and chaos terrain visible on the surface.
